Queueing-based research on web-server load balancing has also analysed routing policies, 
considering measures such as waiting time and request rejection under finite server capacity [4]. 
This is relevant to the project because a thread pool and backend connection limits introduce finite 
resources and queues into the system. 
1.2.3 Concurrency and Operating-System Mechanisms 
Research on web-server concurrency distinguishes synchronous and asynchronous approaches and 
shows that concurrency mechanisms provided by the underlying operating system affect 
performance and implementation complexity

Process/thread scheduling The OS schedules worker threads while the application performs a second-
level scheduling decision for backend servers. 
Synchronization Shared backend state and counters require mutexes to avoid race conditions.  
Producer-consumer problem The acceptor produces tasks while worker threads consume them from a 
bounded queue.

study

Critical sections Backend selection and connection-count updates must be kept consistent. 
Blocking I/O Socket reads and writes block worker threads; this directly affects effective 
concurrency. 
Resource management Thread count, queue size, sockets and backend connections are finite 
resources.

1.4 Identified Research Gap 
The surveyed literature provides substantial analysis of load-balancing algorithms and distributed 
load sharing, but much of the evaluation treats the load balancer primarily as a scheduling or 
network component.We identified an opportunity to connect these scheduling decisions explicitly 
with the internal OS mechanisms used to execute them. 
• Many algorithm comparisons focus on the final network metrics (throughput, latency or 
utilization) without making thread-management overhead a central experimental variable.

This project designed and implemented a multithreaded HTTP load balancer in C that accepts 
concurrent client requests, forwards them to multiple backend servers, and manages server 
selection.It supports Round Robin and Least Connections through a pluggable scheduling 
interface.It also includes a bounded thread pool for concurrent request processing, periodic 
backend health checks, automatic failover and server recovery, request logging, performance 
statistics, and a live dashboard that compares the two algorithms side by side.
